question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-6y &=-8\\ -4x+24y &=40.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -6 & -8 \\ -4 & 24 & 40 \end{bmatrix}
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -6 & -8 \\ -4 & 24 & 40 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -6 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 8 \end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-6y &=-8\\ 0x+0y &=8.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=8$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=8,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+4y &=-8\\ 2x+8y &=-16.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & -8 \\ 2 & 8 & -16 \end{bmatrix}
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & -8 \\ 2 & 8 & -16 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+4y &=-8\\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+4y=-8.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-4y-8,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-4y-8\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -4y-8 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
